title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: An exposure written the other way
summary: Kotlin writes the same pairing two ways. val x = _x.asStateFlow() was recognised; val state get() = _state.asStateFlow() was not, so the backing field looked unexposed.

highlights.title: Readers found again
highlights.description: The count looked for collectors of the private backing, which nothing collects, and read 0 readers on a state the screen collects every time it draws.

highlights.title: 141 exposures, now 143
highlights.description: Measured on a real project of 166 states with a backing field. Of the 23 that still show none, all 23 genuinely have none.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: An exposure written with an accessor is recognised, with or without a declared type.
An accessor pointing at a different state is still not an exposure: the end of line guard holds.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The changelog entry for 1.42.188 said this lens had no tests. It had two files of them; what had none was the modifier list. The line is corrected.
